A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fiddler and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A-F. Their text, algorithms, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original inference benchmarks in Section 4, plus microbenchmarks, sparsity analysis, dataset sensitivity and additional model evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices A-F.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same CPU/GPU execution selection, expert placement and specialized CPU kernel. The changed plot labels identify the same proposed system.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ShareGPT and LMSYS-Chat-1M conversation data and retain the same single-request generation, long-prefill and beam-search scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: DeepSpeed-MII, Mixtral-Offloading (Eliseev and Mazur) and llama.cpp in the main comparisons; llama.cpp for beam search; and DeepSpeed-MII for Phi-3.5-MoE.

E3.justification: Section 4.1, Table 1 and the appendices retain the same hardware, model configurations, precision, sampling procedures, input/output lengths, beam widths and latency metrics.

E4.justification: The microbenchmarks, sparsity analysis, expert-popularity analysis, dataset sensitivity study and latency breakdown in Appendices A-D and F are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix A retains 32 workload executions, one per Mixtral layer, with averages and standard deviations. Figure 7's uncertainty display and the other statistical reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results are retained, including the reported 1.26-fold single-batch and 11.57-fold beam-search speedups. Changes to figure legends and rendering do not change result entries or trends.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same constant GPU-latency and linear CPU-latency assumptions and execution comparison. No mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about heterogeneous CPU/GPU orchestration and performance across single-batch, long-prefill and beam-search inference.

C2.justification: The execution tradeoffs, assumption that non-expert weights fit GPU memory, sparsity limitations and interpretations of dataset robustness and model applicability are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware specifications, baseline versions and configuration parameters remain identical. Both versions provide the same code-access link.

R1.justification: Section 2, the citations and the bibliography are unchanged, as is the positioning against offloading, CPU-based inference and model-compression approaches.

P1.justification: Plot legends change the system name from Twiddler to Fiddler, matching the existing text. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; prose, headings and document organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 4-6 and 9-12 receive corrected system-name legends. Appendix plots also show small typography, spacing and styling adjustments, including a different green shade in Figure 9. No figures or tables are added, removed or relocated.

improvement.justification: Replacing Twiddler with Fiddler in Figures 4-6 and 9-12 resolves a repeated inconsistency between the plots and text, making result attribution clearer. This is a limited presentation improvement; the scientific methods, evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
